title: Account, trial and license
summary: Signing in, the free trial, buying a license, and what each locked screen means.

sections.heading: Two builds
items: Direct download build: you sign in once with Google, Apple, LinkedIn or GitHub in a system sign-in window. The account service records a free trial start once per account and, after purchase, your license.
Mac App Store build: a one-time paid app verified by Apple with no account, no trial and no license key. Account and work-email features are not part of it.

sections.heading: Trial
paragraphs: The trial banner at the top shows the days left. It turns amber for the last three days, and you can dismiss it for the session. Upgrade opens the seat picker. The trial start is kept by the account service, not on this Mac, so deleting files does not restart it.

sections.heading: Buying
paragraphs: Pricing is per seat per year, before tax, and the Upgrade panel shows the current table and your total. Continue to checkout opens Stripe in your browser. Payment happens there, not in the app. When you return, the license is checked again as the window regains focus.

sections.heading: Offline and expiry
paragraphs: The app keeps a signed entitlement on this Mac that is valid for at most seven days and refreshes it when online. If it expires while you are offline, the workspace locks until you verify again. A clock set earlier than a time the app has already seen shows This Mac's clock looks wrong. An account can be active on a limited number of Macs.

sections.heading: Locked screens
paragraphs: Sign in to continue, Your free trial has ended, License needs to be verified online, License no longer active, and This license could not be verified all block the workspace. Verify license again re-checks with the account service. On every one of them, your local evidence on this Mac is not deleted.

sections.heading: Account menu
items: Shows your email, sign-in provider and plan. Profile settings opens the local profile.

Manage subscription (shown once licensed) opens Stripe's billing portal in your browser to change seats or payment method, or to cancel. Cancelling stops renewal at the end of the current billing period: the license stays active until that date, nothing is refunded for the remainder, and the next check after it ends locks the workspace until you subscribe again.

Seats (shown once licensed) assigns the extra seats of an organization purchase. Enter a colleague's email address; no mail is sent. They sign in to OnRecord Studio with that address and the seat is theirs at their first license check, once their sign-in provider has confirmed the address. Your own seat is implicit and not counted. Revoke locks their workspace at their next check and frees the seat; their local evidence is never deleted. Only the purchaser sees seats to manage; a seat holder sees a note saying so.
Sign out clears the local sign-in and returns to the sign-in screen.

Delete account deletes your license account on the server and removes local sign-in data. It does not delete local evidence, and a trial already used on this device is not restored. The result screen states which parts finished.

title: Updates
summary: How the app finds and installs a signed update.

paragraphs: In the direct download build the app checks for an update at start and about every 24 hours. When one is available a notice in the header shows the version and release notes. Install and restart downloads it, installs it and relaunches. Later hides the notice for that version until you restart the app. Your license and account are not affected by an update.

sections.heading: Details
items: Updates are verified against a signing key built into the app before they are installed.
The check contacts updates.writerslogic.com with the app's current version, operating system target and architecture in the request address.
The Mac App Store build has no updater and updates through the App Store.
If an install fails the notice says so and offers Retry install.

paragraphs: This copy of OnRecord Studio updates through the Mac App Store. It has no updater of its own and makes no update checks.

title: Data handling: what stays and what leaves
summary: Privacy in full: exactly what stays on your Mac and each thing that is sent elsewhere.

paragraphs: Nothing here says that nothing is sent. Some features contact other servers. This is the full list for this copy of the app. Details of each are in the topics linked below.

sections.heading: Stays on your Mac
items: Documents you ingest, their extracted text, search indexes, findings, tables, SQL results, the entity graph, and analysis. The app reads and analyzes them locally.
Your profile, tracked requests and confirmed dates, imported notification emails (read on this device only, attachments never opened), briefing outlines, request and appeal drafts, and case files.
The command palette Ask feature. It uses phrase matching on local data and makes no network call.
Activity logs, which reset when you quit.

sections.heading: Sent to the WritersLogic account service (auth.writerslogic.com)
items: Sign-in: you choose Google, Apple, LinkedIn or GitHub, and sign in through that provider. The account service receives the identity your provider releases, including your email address. The sign-in session is kept in the macOS Keychain.

Trial and license: each check sends a signed request with your session, a device public key and a signature made with the device key. The service records the trial start and your plan. It receives no documents or findings.
Checkout: a request for a checkout session with your seat count. Payment itself happens at Stripe in your browser.
Delete account: a request that deletes your account record.
Work-email verification: the full email address you type is sent so a code can be emailed to it, and the code you enter is sent back. Only the domain is kept on this Mac afterwards.

sections.heading: Sent to Apple
items: Purchase verification: at launch, and when you choose to verify again, macOS asks the App Store to confirm this Mac’s purchase of the app. No account service of ours is involved, and no documents or findings are sent.

sections.heading: Sent to the AI provider you choose (autonomous research only)
items: If you use OpenAI or OpenRouter, excerpts of public records you collected, query results and case questions are sent to that provider using your API key. The app masks personal information it detects in the passages it prepares, which is best effort.

It is off until you enable it in Research settings, and then needs a key in your environment or ~/.env. You can turn it off again, or choose Local Ollama, which stays on this Mac. See Autonomous research.

sections.heading: Sent to the AI provider you choose (autonomous research only)
items: If you use OpenAI or OpenRouter, excerpts of public records you collected, query results and case questions are sent to that provider using your API key. The app masks personal information it detects in the passages it prepares, which is best effort.

It is off until you enable it in Research settings, and then needs an OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY line in ~/Library/Containers/com.onrecord.studio/Data/.env, the only place this App Store copy can read a key from. You can turn it off again, or choose Local Ollama, which stays on this Mac. See Autonomous research.

sections.heading: Fetched from the internet by the app
items: Public web pages, documents and data files at the addresses you add, and rechecks of them on the schedule you set. Those sites can see requests from this Mac.
Automatic collection of primary sources from a built-in list of public publishers, unless you turn it off.
The semantic model files, downloaded the first time the semantic model is initialized. Your documents are not part of that download.

sections.heading: Update checks
items: Update checks (direct download build only), which contact updates.writerslogic.com with the app version, operating system target and architecture.

sections.heading: Never done by the app
items: It does not send records requests, appeals, complaints, emails or briefings to any agency or person. Drafts are text for you to submit yourself.
It does not ask for or store portal logins or passwords.
The app does not include an analytics or advertising service.

sections.heading: Not covered here
paragraphs: What your sign-in provider, Stripe, OpenAI, OpenRouter and the sites you fetch do with data on their side is set by their terms.

sections.heading: Not covered here
paragraphs: What Apple, OpenAI, OpenRouter and the sites you fetch do with data on their side is set by their terms.

title: Research snapshot: query your evidence from Python, R or SQL
summary: A read-only DuckDB file of the evidence projection, with a signed manifest that names the exact corpus state, so a query result can be cited and re-run.

paragraphs: Under San Diego, Collection, coverage and storage, open Research snapshot for outside tools and press Export research snapshot. The app writes a .duckdb file and a .manifest.json beside it in the reports/snapshots folder of its data directory. The app keeps running; the snapshot is a separate file that any DuckDB client can open read-only.

sections.heading: What is in it
items: Tables portals, agencies, requests, statutory_extensions, documents, statutory_violations and findings, each with a stable, documented set of columns, plus snapshot_manifest.

Digests, never content: documents carry the SHA-256 of their file and extracted text, not the text. Request descriptions, reviewer notes and local paths are left out, so a snapshot can be shared without reviewing it for personal information in those fields. Headlines, explanations and quoted citations in findings are included as the inbox shows them.
Counts and confidence exactly as stored: confidence_basis_points is NULL when no confidence was measured, which is not zero.

sections.heading: Citing a result
paragraphs: The manifest records the file's SHA-256, the corpus state digest (over every document's identity and text digest) and the findings digest, signed with this installation's export key. Quote the corpus state digest with any figure you publish: anyone holding a snapshot with the same digest can re-run the query and get the same rows. The signature shows the file is unchanged since export; it does not identify who exported it.

sections.heading: What it does not do
items: It is not live. Changes after export are not in it; export again and compare digests.
It cannot be overwritten. A second export the same second fails rather than replacing a file that may already be cited.
It does not include the semantic index, entity graph, tables you imported for SQL analysis, drafts, tracked requests or case files.
